title: API and integration
covers: HTTP and GraphQL APIs, webhooks, SDK surfaces and connections to third-party services that other software calls.

stakeholders.who: A developer integrating against the API or webhook
cares_about: errors that say what to fix
would_notice: an example in the docs that returns an error
camelCase in one endpoint and snake_case in the next
a list endpoint that returns ten thousand rows

stakeholders.who: Whoever runs the service and reads its logs
cares_about: outgoing calls that time out and retry safely
finding one request in the logs
would_notice: a call that hangs with no timeout
a double charge or record after a retry

stakeholders.who: A security reviewer checking the boundary
cares_about: nothing secret in responses or logs
would_notice: an endpoint that answers without a token
a webhook accepted without a signature check
a stack trace or key in an error body

first_ten_seconds: Copy the first example from the docs and run it: does it work as written?
Send one obviously wrong request: is the error clear and a 4xx?
Call a protected endpoint with no token: is it refused?

checks.claim: A committed contract (OpenAPI, schema or SDL) matches the real behaviour, and the documented examples work when copied.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run every documented example request against the running service and compare the responses with the contract.
checks.evidence_required: The example runs and any difference from the contract.

source.quote: A committed contract file exists and is the source of truth

checks.claim: Bad input gets a 4xx with one consistent error shape that names the field and the problem; no 500 for a client mistake.
checks.how_to_inspect: Send a missing field, a wrong type and an unknown field to each changed endpoint.

source.quote: invalid input returns a clear 4xx with a consistent error envelope

checks.claim: The API is versioned and nothing in a shipped version was removed, renamed or made stricter.
checks.how_to_inspect: Diff the contract against the last shipped version and list every removal, rename and new required field.
checks.evidence_required: The contract diff against the last shipped version.

source.quote: Explicit versioning present; no breaking change inside a shipped version.

checks.claim: Names, casing, date formats (ISO 8601 with timezone) and pagination look the same on every endpoint.
checks.how_to_inspect: Put the response of two different endpoints side by side and compare casing, dates and list shape.
checks.evidence_required: The two responses and any mismatch fixed.

source.rationale: Every inconsistency becomes a special case in every client; integrators notice it on the second endpoint.

checks.claim: List endpoints paginate with a documented limit and never return an unbounded list.
checks.how_to_inspect: Call each list endpoint with no parameters on a large dataset and check the size and the next-page link.
checks.evidence_required: The response size and pagination fields.

checks.claim: Hitting the rate limit returns 429 with Retry-After, so a client knows when to try again.
checks.how_to_inspect: Send requests above the limit and read the status and headers of the first refused one.
checks.evidence_required: The refused response with its headers.

checks.claim: Every outgoing call has a timeout and a bounded retry with backoff, and permanent failures go to a dead-letter or alert.
checks.how_to_inspect: Point one dependency at a slow or failing stub and watch the timeout, the retries and where the failure ends up.
checks.evidence_required: The log of the stubbed failure.

checks.claim: Retrying an unsafe write (same idempotency key or event id) creates no second record, charge or message.
checks.how_to_inspect: Send the same write twice with the same key and count the records created.
checks.evidence_required: Both responses and the record count (one).

checks.claim: Each request can be followed end to end in the logs by a request or correlation id, with its outcome and duration.
checks.how_to_inspect: Make one request and find all its log lines by its id.
checks.evidence_required: The log lines for that one request.

source.rationale: Without an id to search, the operator cannot connect a customer's complaint to the failing call.

checks.claim: Every protected route refuses a missing, expired or wrong-scope token, proven by a negative test.
checks.how_to_inspect: Call each protected endpoint without a token and with a token of the wrong scope.
checks.evidence_required: The refusals (401/403) and the negative test that asserts them.

source.quote: a negative (unauthenticated / wrong-scope) test proves rejection

checks.claim: Every inbound webhook verifies its signature on the raw body, and a forged or replayed event is rejected.
checks.how_to_inspect: Send one correctly signed test event and one with a changed body or signature.
checks.evidence_required: The accepted and the rejected responses (N/A when there are no inbound webhooks).

source.quote: Webhook auth / signature verification on every inbound webhook.

checks.claim: No secret, stack trace or personal data appears in responses, error bodies or logs.
checks.how_to_inspect: Trigger a server error and read the response body and the log line it produced.
checks.evidence_required: The error response and the log line.

source.quote: never in responses, error bodies or logs

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: the README example returns 400 because a field was renamed
a missing field crashes the handler instead of returning a 4xx
an error body that shows file paths and line numbers to the caller
a timeout and a retry create two orders
